perspective: COO of a satisfied mid-size DAF sponsor / community foundation
target_claim_or_section: §5 positioning hypotheses 1-3 (verifiable migration, replayable vetting, licence-not-capture)
challenge: From my seat none of the three lines answers a problem I have. 'Your migration with full history and a published exit price' is only relevant once I have already decided to leave, so it cannot create the decision. 'Eligibility decisions you can replay for an auditor' solves a problem my auditor has never raised: my vetting runs on GuideStar/Candid plus an OFAC check and gets a clean opinion. 'Licence, not sponsor-of-record capture' is irrelevant to a CF or independent national that is already its own sponsor of record. These are the vendor's differentiators restated as buyer benefits; the package has no evidence that any buyer ranks them.
evidence: 06 §3 marks W01, W04/W05, W09 and W22 as 'Not observed' or 'Unknown' as purchase reasons; 07 §2 says price, exit terms, history loss and SOC issues are 'not observed as stated reasons'; 06 §2 rows for compliance and implementation team rest on 'no competitor documents this', which is absence of a feature rather than demand for it.
proposed_change: Reframe §5 as untested vendor hypotheses ranked below scope and integration, and add a test that asks satisfied non-switchers to rank them against 'nothing'. Drop hypothesis 3 for CF and independent-sponsor segments.

perspective: COO of a satisfied mid-size DAF sponsor / community foundation
target_claim_or_section: V-1 win/loss interviews (sample = 10 sponsors that switched or evaluated)
challenge: The sample contains only movers (the six iPhi exits, AEF, Vermont, CNY, Arizona). The buyer the strategy actually has to convert is someone like me who stayed. A sample made only of switchers cannot measure the inertia that decides the outcome, and the falsification rule (≥6 of 10 naming product capability) can be met or missed without telling you anything about the roughly 90% of sponsors who never move (51 of 57 iPhi sponsors stayed). Recruiting will also be biased: recent switchers are still in vendor honeymoons or still angry about the migration.
evidence: 22 V-1 method; 07 §1 iPhi attrition 6 of 57, with 1 of 26 national/faith; trackC-switches.csv S39 (Commonwealth STAY) is the only non-switch row.
proposed_change: Split V-1 into 5 switchers and at least 5 stayers, including sponsors on NPact and Ren that sat through forced events and still did not switch, and ask stayers what would have made them consider leaving. Add a stayer-based rule, for example thesis weakened if fewer than 2 of 5 stayers would take a meeting at their next renewal.

perspective: COO of a satisfied mid-size DAF sponsor / community foundation
target_claim_or_section: §2 'integrated platform' as the observed, stated switch trigger (Vermont, CNY, Arizona)
challenge: The 'stated reason' rests on three sponsor communications, two of which are donor-facing service notices ('new integrated software that will help us serve you better') and one a vendor-hosted case study. Those are after-the-fact explanations written to justify a disruption to donors, not procurement criteria. 24 of the 44 switch rows say 'not stated'. The real reasons at most CFs are mundane: the vendor sunset or forced a re-host, a new CEO or CFO arrived, the auditor flagged reconciliation, or peers at a CF conference recommended Foundant. Calling integration 'VERIFIED' overstates what a donor notice can establish.
evidence: trackC-switches.csv: 24/44 rows reason_stated = 'not stated'; S18 reason is boilerplate from a sponsor notice; S04 and S06/S07 reasons come from vendor-hosted case studies ('sponsor self-report'); 07 §2 classes leadership change as 'plausible; unmeasured'.
proposed_change: Reclassify integration as 'stated in public communications (n=3)', not a verified purchase trigger, and add peer referral and leadership turnover as candidate triggers V-1 must test.

perspective: COO of a satisfied mid-size DAF sponsor / community foundation
target_claim_or_section: §1-§2 switching cost framed mainly as data-migration risk
challenge: The package treats switching cost as a data problem (mapping, reconciliation, freeze days). For me most of the cost is people and institutions. My staff need 6-12 months to reach proficiency on a new system. I lose year-end giving season, so the window is really Feb-Sep. Every advisor and donor login, saved recurring grant and report has to be re-learned. The finance committee and board have to approve. My auditor has to re-test controls on a new system, which means first-year audit fee uplift and a SOC 1 reliance gap. Insurance and cyber questionnaires get redone. None of this is reduced by a Merkle-sealed staging area. The sponsors in the switch log tolerated 2-9 week freezes, which suggests the data piece is not the binding constraint.
evidence: trackC-switches.csv S18 (~3.5 weeks suspended), S19 (~9 weeks), S17 (~6 weeks), S30 (~5.5 weeks), S12 (~2 weeks): sponsors accepted long freezes and switched anyway. 06 §4 item 3 counts TCO $170k-846k, but 08 has no line for staff retraining, auditor re-testing or board time.
proposed_change: Add a non-data switching-cost model (staff retraining hours, audit fee uplift and control re-testing, board cycles, donor and advisor support load, seasonality blackout) and state which parts Unbound can actually reduce. Expect the answer to be 'little', and say so.

perspective: COO of a satisfied mid-size DAF sponsor / community foundation
target_claim_or_section: §2-§3 entrant viability (G1-G2 capital $0.7-5M; no SOC history)
challenge: My biggest objection is not your product but whether you will exist in five years. DAF records must be kept for at least seven years and donor relationships last decades. The package itself documents vendor churn (DonorFirst, Pinkaloo, iPhi, Vennfi, Giving Place all acquired; Give Interactive loss-making with abandoned implementations; Blackbaud divesting FIMS). A startup funded stage by stage with go/no-go gates explicitly built to 'pause the thesis' is exactly the vendor my board will veto. 06 admits the infosec disadvantage but never models vendor viability as a purchase blocker. Escrow is a weak mitigant for hosted SaaS: transitions are hard in practice and release conditions get disputed.
evidence: trackC-switches.csv S01, S02, S11, S21, S22, S23, S44 (vendor ownership events); 06 §1 Give Interactive W16 viability; 16 §6 'thesis is paused'; legal commentary: SaaS escrow transitions harder than contracts imply (legaldive.com/news/saas-escrow-generalcounsel-kesslen-satlin-lowenstein-sandler/630319; saastr.com on startup vendor failure).
proposed_change: Add vendor-viability risk as an explicit purchase blocker in 06 §2 and 07 §4. Specify mitigants buyers would credit: partner or parent balance sheet, a hosted-data transition-services clause, a funded runway disclosure and a named fallback operator. Note that licence-via-channel (G2) partly fixes this only if the channel partner carries the risk.

perspective: COO of a satisfied mid-size DAF sponsor / community foundation
target_claim_or_section: §3 minimum viable entry point = a PAID migration assessment
challenge: I would not pay for an assessment of a migration I have not decided to do, especially when every vendor I would actually choose will scope my conversion for free during the sales cycle. Foundant documents a standard migration-site validation process as part of implementation, and the package itself says free migration is table stakes in nonprofit CRM. 08 §6 also contradicts 16 §3: 08 prices T0-T1 free and T2-T3 paid, while 16 calls the paid assessment the minimum viable commercial entry and sets the G1 exit at ≥2 paying customers. A paid T2-T3 needs a DPA and real data, which a satisfied sponsor will not hand to an unproven vendor before deciding to leave.
evidence: 08 §1 last row 'Free migration offers: table stakes (CLM-021)'; 08 §6 'Price T0-T1 free, T2-T3 paid'; 08 §3 says real-record loading needs a data processing agreement; Foundant support docs on CSData migration and validation as part of implementation (support.foundant.com/hc/en-us/articles/14281082342423; /13058740806295).
proposed_change: Reconcile 08 and 16: make the assessment free (T0-T1) and treat paid T2-T3 as an implementation deposit for sponsors that have already decided to switch. Remove the 'paid assessment' wedge as a revenue claim and count its cost as CAC.

perspective: COO of a satisfied mid-size DAF sponsor / community foundation
target_claim_or_section: §3 'contract-end back-schedule' and 16/22 V-5 'contract-end windows' (≥10 windows in 24 months)
challenge: A contract end is not a window for a satisfied customer. Most of my vendor agreements auto-renew, and the notice date is the point where I use a competitor quote to renegotiate price, not to leave. An entrant that turns up at my notice date mostly becomes free leverage for my incumbent. V-5 counts windows from 990 payments and DNS, which shows when a contract could end but not whether the buyer is in-market. 06 §4 names auto-renewal as a lock-in mechanic yet the strategy still treats the calendar as pipeline. Real windows are the forced ones (sunset, divestiture, re-host), and the log shows the incumbent or Foundant is already positioned when those happen.
evidence: 06 §4 item 5 'auto-renewal, notice windows'; trackC-notes.md line 121; 06 §3 W21 'Partly'; trackC-switches.csv S08/S15 forced events (AEF picked Ren, not a newcomer, S26); S30 Greater Washington CF re-signed with NPact despite NPact's 3-yr term and 90-day notice.
proposed_change: Change the V-5 pass rule from 'windows exist' to 'buyers in window confirm active evaluation'. Track the conversion rate from window to RFP to non-incumbent award, and count competitor quotes used for renegotiation as a failure mode.

perspective: COO of a satisfied mid-size DAF sponsor / community foundation
target_claim_or_section: §3 W02/W03/W20, W01, W25 and §2 donor row (freeze, history, grant delays as opportunities)
challenge: The research catalogues donor and charity pain (freezes, re-registration, truncated history, slow grants) and then concedes in 07 §4 that this pain does not change purchasing. The matrix still lists these as places 'Unbound can solve', and they reappear as positioning line 1. As the buyer, donor complaints reach me as a handful of service tickets. They show up as purchase reasons only when donors leave, and the only donor-level movement in the log (S40) is a Low-confidence inference from forums at a national sponsor that is not in the target segment. Sponsor-level purchase reasons are cost, staff workload, audit findings, board risk and vendor stability. The package mixes the two in the same matrix.
evidence: 07 §4 'Solving user pain does not ... change purchasing behaviour'; 06 §3 W02/W03/W20 'Not observed as a reason' but 'Partly' solvable; trackC-switches.csv S40 confidence Low, evidence class INFERENCE; S26 AEF accepted a 2-year history truncation and still chose Ren.
proposed_change: Split the matrix into donor-felt pain and sponsor purchase reasons. Remove donor-pain items from positioning unless V-1 shows a sponsor citing donor attrition, and use S26 as a counter-example to the history-loss pitch.

perspective: COO of a satisfied mid-size DAF sponsor / community foundation
target_claim_or_section: §3 'Lower and published price with symmetric exit' and §5 exit symmetry as a 'cheap credibility signal'
challenge: Price is not a lever for me. Platform fees are a small line next to staff cost and investment fees, and DAF admin fees are passed through to fundholders anyway. A lower price from a startup reads as a viability risk, not a saving. Exit symmetry signals that you expect customers to leave. My counsel will want transition services and data return clauses, which the incumbent will match the moment I ask; the package rates replication as 'Trivial'. A differentiator the incumbent can copy in a renewal redline is a negotiating chip for me, not a reason to switch.
evidence: 06 §3 W04/W05 and W11 'Incumbent replication: Trivial', 'Changes purchasing: Not observed / No evidence'; 07 §5 'no DAF evidence that it wins deals'; 16 §6 last bullet acknowledges competitors can ship it first (HYP-013).
proposed_change: Demote price and exit symmetry to hygiene factors. Remove them from the reasons to choose, and model them as concessions the incumbent will make at renewal.

perspective: COO of a satisfied mid-size DAF sponsor / community foundation
challenge: The G0 budget is stated inconsistently. 16 §2 gives G0 as $0.15-0.35M. 22 §1 says the G0 tests (V-1, V-2, V-3, V-5, V-6, V-9) total about $0.07-0.25M, but the listed costs sum to $65k-220k. The gap matters little in dollars but signals that the plan has no budget for the main cost of reaching satisfied buyers: senior sales time and conference presence to earn meetings with COOs who are not looking.
proposed_change: Reconcile the figures and add an explicit buyer-access line (sales headcount, CF and NPT conference presence, referral incentives) to G0 and G1, since recruiting stayers for V-1 and V-2 will cost more than recruiting switchers.
